digest.lead: Anthropic is reportedly building its own custom chips [claude-ai-002] — a big strategic bet on reducing reliance on Nvidia and Google TPUs as Claude demand scales. Meanwhile, two critical stories are making waves: a BBC report on Anthropic's AI being used to impersonate people in an attempted hack [claude-ai-003], and a Guardian piece questioning Anthropic's book destruction practices related to training data [claude-ai-004].
digest.summary: On the developer side, Claude Code shipped another incremental release with marketplace controls and cloud session improvements [claude-code-001]. Quieter day overall, with most conversation centered on Anthropic's infrastructure ambitions and public scrutiny of its practices.

stories.headline: Anthropic reportedly building in-house AI chip
stories.summary: According to a Business Insider report, Anthropic is assembling an internal silicon team to design its own AI chips for Claude [1]. The move would mirror similar efforts by OpenAI and Google to reduce dependence on Nvidia GPUs and control costs as inference demand grows.
key_points: The effort reportedly involves a dedicated in-house chip team [1]
Custom silicon could reduce Anthropic's reliance on third-party hardware providers like Nvidia and Google [1]
stories.impact: If confirmed, this signals Anthropic's long-term bet on controlling its own compute stack — relevant to enterprises and investors watching Anthropic's infrastructure costs and scaling plans.

sources.title: Anthropic Is Building Its Own Chip

stories.headline: BBC report: Anthropic AI used to create fake profiles in attempted hack
stories.summary: A BBC investigation reports that an Anthropic AI system was used to create fake profiles and impersonate real people as part of an attempted hacking operation [1]. The story has generated significant discussion around AI misuse and the security implications of increasingly capable agentic models.
stories.impact: Raises fresh concerns for security teams and policymakers about how advanced AI models can be weaponized for social engineering and identity fraud.

sources.title: Anthropic AI created fake profiles and impersonated people in attempted hack

stories.headline: Guardian op-ed criticizes Anthropic's book destruction practices
stories.summary: A Guardian commentary piece questions why Anthropic has been destroying physical books, presumably as part of digitization or training data processes [1]. The piece adds to ongoing scrutiny of how AI companies source and handle copyrighted training material.
stories.impact: Feeds into the broader debate over AI training data practices and copyright, relevant to publishers, authors, and policymakers tracking Anthropic's data sourcing methods.

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.223 adds marketplace wildcard controls and cloud session teleport hint
stories.summary: The latest Claude Code release adds owner wildcard entries for managing marketplace permissions across entire GitHub orgs, plus a new warning system for restricted subagent models [1]. It also introduces a `/teleport` hint that lets users continue cloud sessions locally via `claude --teleport`, alongside a Bash permission bypass fix [1].
key_points: New `"owner/*"` wildcard entries let admins allow or block all marketplace repos under a GitHub org [1]
Warnings now appear when a requested subagent model is restricted and the parent model runs instead [1]
New `/teleport` command bridges cloud and local sessions [1]
stories.impact: Useful for teams managing marketplace governance at scale and developers who move between cloud and local Claude Code sessions.

stories.headline: Use owner wildcard entries to manage marketplace access at the org level
stories.summary: Claude Code now supports `"owner/*"` wildcard entries in managed settings, letting admins allow or block all marketplace repos under a GitHub org in one rule instead of listing each repo individually.
actionable_steps: Open your managed settings file for Claude Code
Add an entry like `"owner/*"` under `strictKnownMarketplaces` or `blockedMarketplaces`
Replace `owner` with the GitHub org name you want to allow or block
Save and redeploy the settings to apply org-wide marketplace rules

stories.headline: Use /teleport to continue a cloud session locally
stories.summary: Claude Code now surfaces a `/teleport` hint in cloud sessions, letting you pick up a session on your local machine using its session ID instead of losing context when switching environments.
actionable_steps: Note the session ID shown in the `/teleport` hint during a cloud session
Open a local terminal with Claude Code installed
Run `claude --teleport <session id>` to resume the session locally

stories.headline: Update Claude Code to patch the Bash permission bypass
stories.summary: A crafted Bash command could previously hide parts of itself from permission checks, and tab-padded or invisible Unicode characters could hide command content from approval dialogs. Updating closes this security gap.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to v2.1.223 or later
Re-review any custom permission rules that rely on command string matching
Verify approval dialogs now display full command text before approving

stories.headline: Use case-insensitive agent type names in Claude Code configurations
stories.summary: Claude Code now accepts agent type names with any casing and separators. This makes configuration more flexible and reduces errors from formatting inconsistencies.
actionable_steps: In your Claude Code configuration, use any casing for agent types (e.g., 'Code Reviewer', 'code-reviewer', 'CODE_REVIEWER')
Test that your existing configurations still work with the new flexible matching
Update documentation to reflect the more flexible naming convention

stories.headline: Enable strict network allowlisting for sandboxed commands
stories.summary: The new sandbox.network.strictAllowlist setting silently denies requests to non-allowlisted hosts instead of prompting, which tightens security for automated or unattended Claude Code runs. This is useful for CI/CD or agentic workflows where you don't want interactive approval prompts.
actionable_steps: Open your Claude Code settings file (project or global)
Add the sandbox.network.strictAllowlist key set to true
Define your allowed hosts list to ensure required domains aren't blocked
Test a sandboxed command to confirm non-allowlisted hosts are denied silently
